_comment: The automation dial. Each feature has a risk tier; the tier decides who signs, whether a hand security review is required, how far Bob may run on its own, and who approves a release to production.
Governance-protected like approvers.json: change it only in a chore(SDD) commit reviewed by the code owners. Pipelines read it from the target branch, so a change cannot approve itself.
node sdd/scripts/policy.mjs check   validates this file. Some gates are locked: the check fails if a setting would remove a human decision the organisation must keep (see 'locked' below).
Roles are the ones in approvers.json: business-owner, business-analyst, architect, developer, appsec.

1.label: Critical
1.means: Can move money or other value, guards access or credentials, or changes security settings.

2.label: Sensitive
2.means: Shows or stores personal or confidential data, but moves no value.

3.label: Standard
3.means: Moves no value, holds no credentials, adds no personal data.

alwaysAutomated: Commit rules G1–G10 (in Bob, in the git hook and again in the pipeline)
SonarQube scan of production code before any testing step
Pipeline check that every sign-off was made by a listed person with the right role
locked: Every tier needs a human plan sign-off and a human phase sign-off. No tier can hand them to Bob or the pipeline.
Tier 1 plans and phases are signed by the business owner only.
The developer role never signs plans or phases (the maker is never the checker).
Tier 1 and 2 features always get a hand security review.
Bob runs tier 1 features one step at a time.
Accepting a security risk (a waiver) is always AppSec's decision.
Change requests are always decided by the business owner.
Every release to production needs a person; tier 1 needs two people with different roles.
Nobody signs their own work unless the repository is marked as a training repository.
